scope: Ordinary Character/Enemy block-radius defaults, current attribute multiplier and Trap/GiantTrap exceptions. Reuses existing Blocking instruction artifacts and adds bounded constant/schema witnesses. No client execution, live XLua audit or gameplay-wide census.

floatConstants.name: characterDefaultBlockRadiusScale
floatConstants.use: Character.get_defaultBlockRadiusScale[75927] movss at0x180a39fe8; Enemy corresponding getter reads same address

floatConstants.name: flyRadius
floatConstants.use: Character.get__blockRadius default FLY path and BlockRadiusManager multiplication operand

ordinaryCharacterDefaults.defaultSource: DLL constants in ordinary Character and Enemy getters, not a per-character prefab radius field

conclusions.currentScalePath: For FLY only, HookBlockRadius reads current Attributes.GetValue(BLOCK_RADIUS_SCALE=37), compares with defaultBlockRadiusScale, and GetBlockRadius multiplies 0.8944 by the current value when hooked. WALK uses the fixed ordinary WALK radius.
conclusions.dataSchema: AttributesData contains a separate blockRadiusScale ObscuredFloat field. This is an attribute-data field, distinct from a directly configured final radius.
exceptions: Trap.get_blockRadiusSquare reads the instance float field _blockRadiusSquare(+0x57c).
GiantTrap.get_blockRadiusSquare returns the ordinary WALK square constant, while CheckInBlockRange checks multiple stored position origins.

limits: The DLL/metadata fingerprints match the referenced existing native instruction evidence; active XLua replacements and actual runtime effects were not audited.
Presence of AttributesData.blockRadiusScale establishes the native data item; this extraction does not inventory per-unit serialized values, modules, buffs, or their actual gameplay use.

No claim that every blocker shares Character defaults, that every character independently configures a radius, or that a specific Core/Content field design follows automatically from these native facts.
This package does not re-evaluate the previously noted uncertainty in FLY old-relation revalidation after attribute changes.
